newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FRANCE'S LE PEN SLAMS "GLOBALISATION" THROUGH EU.
newsitem.headline: FRANCE'S LE PEN SLAMS "GLOBALISATION" THROUGH EU.

text.p: French nationalist politician Jean-Marie Le Pen spoke against globalisation at the biggest Hungarian rally in years, organised by an extreme right-wing party.

"Globalisation...aims at destroying the nations, our humanist and Christian civilisation," Le Pen told an enthusiastic crowd estimated at between 20,000 and 30,000 people outside the Hungarian parliament.
The crowd was much larger than those which attended ceremonies earlier this week marking Hungary's doomed 1956 uprising against Soviet rule.
"It (the uprising) was crushed amidst indifference and cowardice of the Western powers," Le Pen said.
After paying tribute to the uprising, he defended strong nation states against globalisation.
While admitting that European countries need a harmonic relationship, said he is opposed to the European Union and supports De Gaulle's ideal of strong nation states.
"The Europe of Maastricht, a federal Europe is just a step towards globalisation and it deliberately drives towards the destruction of nation states," Le Pen said.
He was invited by the rally's organiser, extreme right-wing politician Istvan Csurka and his Hungarian Justice and Life Party (MIEP).

Csurka's party which failed to get into parliament in the 1994 elections, can gathers sizeable crowds from a population hit by Hungary's transition to market economy that brought two-figure inflation, a ten percent jobless rate and decreasing real wages.
"Who else can bring so many people to the streets in Hungary as we do?" asked Csurka the crowd which chanted anti-government slogans.
In his address he spoke against the privatisation process, lately surrounded by controversy and allegations of corruption.
"After selling cheap all they could, they (the ruling parties) now haggle over the remaining bits," Csurka said.
He called for all national forces inside and outside parliament to unite against the coalition.
The crowd demanded the present Socialist-Liberal coalition's resignation but was more opposed to the junior coalition partner Liberal Democrats than to the Socialists.
"We are the real oppostion, not those sitting in Parliament, who had all been bribed by the coalition," MIEP party member Peter Kuruc told Reuters.
The last anti-government rally with an over 10,000-strong attendance was also organised by MIEP last October, on the eve of 1956 celebrations.
